facts.text: Thomas Jefferson named Capitol Hill in 1793, echoing Rome’s Capitoline Hill and the Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
The Folger Shakespeare Library, built on former brick townhouses, houses the world’s largest Shakespeare collection and a renowned theatre.
Capitol Hill is the oldest residential neighborhood in Washington, dating back to the original city plan by Pierre‑Charles L’Enfant.
After the Civil War, middle‑class workers spurred the construction of row houses that still line the streets of Capitol Hill today.
The Capitol Complex on Capitol Hill includes the U.S. Capitol, the Supreme Court, the Library of Congress, and the Marine Barracks.
Before becoming a landmark, the site of Capitol Hill once hosted livestock, as Thomas Jenkins noted a thick wood cover in 1791.
